channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan to implement six waste-to-energy projects by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing six investment projects to improve waste management and produce electricity from waste by 2026-2027. The total cost is $933 million, with Chinese companies involved. These projects aim to process 3.6 million tons of waste annually, generating 1.6 billion kWh of electricity.

item.title: Uzbekistan to host first Central Asian Student Sports Forum in October 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan will host the first Central Asian Student Sports Forum from September 29 to October 2, 2026. The event aims to promote Uzbekistan's experience in student sports development internationally and strengthen cooperation among Central Asian nations. FISU president Leonz Eder will attend.

item.title: Tashkent's modernist architecture added to UNESCO World Heritage List
item.description: Uzbekistan's nomination 'Modernist Architecture of Tashkent' has been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, marking the first national inclusion in 25 years. This recognition highlights 10 key sites and aims to boost cultural tourism and heritage preservation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Using First-Floor Apartments for Business
item.description: Uzbekistan may allow over 46,000 first-floor apartments to be used for commercial purposes without reclassifying them as non-residential. This could create jobs and boost incomes, according to the Ministry of Construction. A new regulation is being developed to simplify the process for opening small businesses like salons or shops.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Approves Alphabet Changes, Adopting 28 Latin-Based Letters
item.description: The Uzbek Senate has approved amendments to the law on the Latin-based Uzbek alphabet. The new alphabet will feature 28 letters and an apostrophe, replacing the current 26 letters and three letter combinations. Documents and currency issued under the old alphabet will remain valid during the transition period.

item.title: Tajikistan Recruits Workers for Jobs in Turkey and Russia
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Labor and Migration is recruiting for jobs in Turkey and Russia. Positions in Turkey include general labor, welding, and mechanics, with salaries from $700-$1250. Russia offers jobs in industry, agriculture, construction, and services, paying 80,000-140,000 rubles. Employers in Turkey provide housing and food, while Russian employers cover migration registration.

item.title: Environmental Inspector Dies While Trying to Stop Illegal Fishing in Syrdarya
item.description: An environmental inspector, Mirzo Botirov, died in the Syrdarya region while attempting to stop individuals engaged in illegal fishing using electric gear. The suspects resisted, causing him to fall into the water. His body was recovered the following day. An investigation is underway, and the deceased will be posthumously awarded the 'Nature Protector' badge.

item.title: Tajik businessman arrested in US for sanctions violations against Russia has been released
item.description: Salimjon Nasriddinov, a Tajik businessman detained in the US nearly three years ago for allegedly sending sanctioned equipment to Russia, has been released. His family declined to provide further details, and the terms of his release are unknown. Nasriddinov had pleaded guilty to the charges in a New York federal court.

item.title: Expert discusses German election results and the rise of the AfD party
item.description: An expert analyzes the recent German federal state elections in Saxony-Anhalt, where the far-right AfD party secured a significant victory with 43.8% of the vote. The article discusses potential coalition scenarios and the implications of the AfD's growing influence on Germany's party system, noting the traditional refusal of major parties to cooperate with the far-right.

item.title: Ecological police officer killed in the line of duty confronting illegal fishing
item.description: An ecological police inspector died while on duty after confronting individuals engaged in illegal fishing using electric seines. The incident occurred when the inspector encountered the offenders resisting his attempts to stop their activity. Further details were not immediately available.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Benefits and Preferences for Entrepreneurs
item.description: A seminar in Surkhandarya discussed a presidential decree offering new benefits for entrepreneurs, including a three-year exemption from inspections for small businesses. The decree aims to reduce state interference and strengthen protections for businesses, fostering economic growth.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Six-Month Licensing for LED Lamp Imports
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a six-month mandatory licensing system for importing LED lamps. The Ministry of Economy and Commerce would issue licenses, requiring prior approval from the Ministry of Energy, to control unregulated imports and support local producers.

item.title: Foreigner Detained at Osh Airport for Suspected Cigarette Smuggling
item.description: A foreign national was apprehended at Osh International Airport on suspicion of smuggling a large quantity of Esse Change cigarettes. The State Committee for National Security reported that a criminal case has been initiated for economic smuggling.

item.title: Tax incentives for electrical engineering companies to be extended until 2030
item.description: Tax incentives for electrical engineering companies are planned to be extended until 2030. A portion of loans allocated for investment projects will be covered for three years.

item.title: Kamchybek Tashiev's defense to appeal Bishkek City Court ruling in 'Letter of 75' case
item.description: The defense team for former State Committee for National Security Chairman Kamchybek Tashiev plans to appeal the Bishkek City Court's ruling in the "Letter of 75" case. Lawyer Ikramidin Aitkulov stated the decision is illegal and unfounded, questioning the reclassification of charges.

item.title: CIS Interpol Bureaus Discuss Cooperation Development in Minsk
item.description: Heads of national Interpol bureaus from CIS member states met in Minsk to discuss cooperation. Delegations from Azerbaijan, China, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, UAE, and Uzbekistan attended. The meeting focused on information exchange, existing problems, and solutions for enhancing regional law enforcement collaboration.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan disburses over 285 million soms for 'Bala Yrysy' child benefit
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has financed another payment of the 'Bala Yrysy' child benefit, totaling 285.59 million soms. The Ministry of Labor reported that 232,229 recipients are now included after database updates. This is an increase of over 40,000 recipients and nearly 50 million soms compared to July's payments.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan court reclassifies charges in 'Letter of 75' case, imposes probation
item.description: The Bishkek City Court reclassified charges in the 'Letter of 75' case from 'Forcible seizure of power' to 'Obstruction of the exercise of electoral rights.' All defendants received a four-year sentence, suspended with two years of probation. This differs from the district court's verdict, which included property confiscation.

item.title: Azerbaijan International Bank acquires 51% stake in Uzbekistan's Davr Bank for $140 million
item.description: Azerbaijan International Bank (ABB) has purchased a 51% stake in the private Davr Bank for approximately $140 million. The transaction, valued at 1.646 trillion soms, occurred on the Tashkent Stock Exchange. This acquisition marks ABB's entry into the Uzbek banking market, as previously announced during a meeting between the presidents of Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Foreigner detained at Osh airport for alleged cigarette smuggling
item.description: A foreign national was detained at Osh International Airport on September 6 for allegedly smuggling a large batch of Esse Change cigarettes. The State Committee for National Security (GKNB) reported the incident. The suspect has been placed in pre-trial detention as an investigation is underway for economic smuggling. The GKNB is working to identify other potential participants in the scheme.

item.title: Uzbekistan aims to increase electrical engineering exports to $5 billion by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to boost its electrical engineering exports to $5 billion by 2030, according to a presentation reviewed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The sector's output has grown significantly, with exports already exceeding $1 billion to 65 countries. The strategy focuses on high-value products, including new items like electric vehicle charging stations and heat pumps.

item.title: Uzbekistan allocates $50 million for copper purchases by electrical engineering firms
item.description: Uzbekistan will allocate $50 million for electrical engineering companies to purchase copper raw materials. Firms will cover 25% of the cost, while 'UzSanoatExport' will finance the remaining 75%. This measure aims to support the growth and export potential of the country's electrical engineering sector.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan showcases investment potential at China's CIFIT international fair
item.description: Kyrgyzstan presented its investment potential at the 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade (CIFIT) in Xiamen. The National Investment Agency highlighted promising sectors and opportunities for joint projects to attract foreign capital.

item.title: Kamchybek Tashiev's defense to appeal Bishkek court's decision
item.description: The defense team for former GKNB head Kamchybek Tashiev plans to appeal the Bishkek City Court's ruling in the 'letter of 75' case. Lawyer Ikramidin Aitkulov stated the decision is illegal and unfounded, citing a change in charges during the proceedings. Tashiev and other defendants disagree with the verdict and will appeal to the Supreme Court.

item.title: Uzbekistan to change official currency exchange rate calculation from September 15
item.description: From September 15, Uzbekistan will alter its official currency exchange rate calculation method. The new system will consider transactions made on the interbank over-the-counter market alongside the exchange.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan 'Letters 75' case: all defendants receive probation, no charges of coup, no asset confiscation
item.description: Defendants in Kyrgyzstan's 'Letters 75' case have been sentenced to four years imprisonment with a two-year probation period. The charges do not include coup attempts, and there will be no confiscation of property.

item.title: Boghdod district to create over 240 new jobs through entrepreneurship development
item.description: The development of entrepreneurship in the Boghdod district is expected to create more than 240 new job opportunities. This initiative aims to boost local economic activity and employment.

item.title: Kazakhstan deputy proposes compensation for car repairs due to poor fuel quality
item.description: A member of the Kurultai proposed strengthening control over petroleum products and establishing a compensation mechanism for citizens affected by low-quality fuel. He cited numerous complaints about AI-95 and AI-98 gasoline damaging car parts. The deputy also suggested stricter state oversight of fuel quality, including unannounced inspections and mandatory laboratory testing.

item.title: 'Letter of 75' case: Court reclassifies charge, imposes two-year probation
item.description: The Bishkek City Court has ruled on the 'letter of 75' case, reclassifying the charge from 'violent seizure of power' to 'obstruction of electoral rights'. This change means property confiscation, previously part of the district court's sentence, is no longer applicable. Several former officials, including Kamchybek Tashiev, received a four-year suspended sentence with three years probation.

item.title: Anti-extremism operation in Chui region yields searches at 48 locations
item.description: Police conducted searches at 48 locations in Kyrgyzstan's Chui region as part of an anti-extremism operation. The searches were linked to criminal cases initiated under Article 332 of the Criminal Code. Authorities seized firearms, ammunition, daggers, and vehicle license plates, which will undergo examination to determine their relevance to the ongoing investigations.

item.title: Uzbek National Guard's core functions to be restructured for public safety
item.description: The core functions of Uzbekistan's National Guard are being restructured, consolidating tasks related to public safety and order. A new law requires National Guard officers to identify themselves when addressing citizens. The Senate has approved these changes.

item.title: Putin: Migration processes generated 321 billion rubles for Russian budget
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that migration processes generated 321 billion rubles in revenue for the state over the past 1.5 years. Over 60 billion rubles went to the federal budget, and over 250-260 billion to regional budgets. Around 100,000 migrants who committed violations were expelled from Russia.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes land transfer for foreign property buyers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a new law requiring foreigners to transfer land ownership to the state when purchasing real estate. The land would be leased back for up to 50 years. This proposal aims to regulate foreign ownership of land associated with properties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan presents investment potential at China International Fair
item.description: Kyrgyzstan showcased its investment potential at the 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade (CIFIT) in Xiamen. The event provided a platform to present investment opportunities, attract capital, and foster collaboration with international businesses and investors.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Criminal Liability for Illegal Underground Tunnels
item.description: Uzbekistan is establishing criminal liability for the construction and use of illegal underground tunnels across its state border. The Senate approved amendments to the Criminal and Criminal Procedure Codes. Senator Qutbiddin Burxonov stated that 12 such tunnels were discovered between 2016-2025, used to smuggle goods worth over $3.7 million and 5 kg of gold.

item.title: Uzbekistan Welcomed 9.1 Million Tourists in First Eight Months of 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan hosted 9.1 million foreign tourists from January to August 2026, a 21.1% increase compared to the same period in 2025. August alone saw nearly 1.5 million visitors. Tourism revenue from services reached $4.6 billion, up 53.5% year-on-year. Significant growth was noted from Asian, US, Russian, and European countries.

item.title: Seven Percent of Kyrgyzstanis Lost Money Due to Cyberattacks, Survey Finds
item.description: A 2025 Financial Literacy Survey by the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan reveals that seven percent of surveyed citizens lost money due to hacking or phishing attacks, up from four percent in 2021. The proportion of respondents who experienced bank card detail theft rose to three percent. Digital financial literacy remains a concern, with 30% unsure how to handle suspicious messages.

item.title: Glaciers in Tajikistan's GBAO Show 1.5-2 Meter Decrease in Level
item.description: An international research expedition in August 2026 on glaciers in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO) recorded a 1.5-2 meter drop in ice levels. The study, involving Tajik scientists and Swiss university representatives, aims to assess glacier dynamics and their role in water resource regulation amid climate change.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to establish international transport and logistics center in Sary-Tash
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Investment Agency and Textile Trans LLC signed a memorandum to create the Sary-Tash international transport and logistics center. The project aims to attract $100 million in investment and enhance Kyrgyzstan's role as a trade hub between China, Central Asia, and South Asia.

item.title: Ombudsman visits prisons, reports inmates have access to medical treatment
item.description: The Ombudsman visited prisons and reported that inmates have access to medical treatment. Ruhshona Hakimbova is learning English, but it remains unclear why the request for surgery for Pirmuhammadzoda's relatives was denied. The article mentions Pirmuhammadzoda is a journalist.
